_meta.indication: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for PET imaging in men with suspected prostate cancer recurrence based on elevated blood PSA levels following prior treatment

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Emory University study R01 (re-analyzed as BED001), published by Schuster et al, J Urol 2014
pivotal_trials.design: Open label, single center, non-randomized comparative study of 18F-Fluciclovine PET imaging with histology (biopsy) as the standard of truth
pivotal_trials.population: Men with suspected recurrence of prostate cancer based on rising PSA levels following radical prostatectomy and/or radiotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Positive Predictive Value (PPV) at subject, lesion and region level, validated against histopathology
pivotal_trials.n: 105 Axumin scans evaluated in comparison to histopathology
pivotal_trials.result: Study met its primary PPV endpoint; at the subject level 7 of 10 (71%) patients with lesions detected by fluciclovine F 18 had prostatic cancer metastases and nearly all (97%) patients with metastases had detections verified as positive by histology

key_safety: Adverse reactions were reported in <=1% of subjects; most common were injection site pain, injection site erythema and dysgeusia. No deaths or serious adverse reactions were reported.
target_moa: Fluciclovine F 18 is a synthetic amino acid taken up across cell membranes by amino acid transporters (LAT-1 and ASCT2) that are upregulated in prostate cancer cells, resulting in greater uptake in prostate cancer cells than in surrounding normal tissue; detected by PET
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (F-18 labeled synthetic amino acid analog)

rems.type: DRISK determined a REMS was not necessary; as a class diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals have not required a REMS, and the applicant did not submit a proposed REMS

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise regulatory or scientific issues and there was regulatory precedent (Choline C 11)

basis.text: Granted priority review because fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review status because Fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome.

summary.text: New molecular entity diagnostic radiopharmaceutical submitted by Blue Earth Diagnostics on September 28, 2015 and granted priority review; approved without an advisory committee meeting and without a REMS. It was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on an Emory University study meeting its primary PPV endpoint.

citations.quote: On September 28, 2015 the Applicant (Blue Earth Diagnostics Ltd) submitted a 505(b)(1) new drug application (NDA) for the new molecular entity Fluciclovine F 18.

The application was granted a priority review status because Fluciclovine F 18 was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome.
